description:
Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship model, claiming it reduces the average cost of completing professional tasks by 62% compared with its predecessor while introducing additional safeguards against offensive cybersecurity capabilities and other high-risk uses.

“According to Work360 — a proprietary benchmark evaluating performance on challenging industry tasks across 721 specialized fields — Qwen4-Max outperforms its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, overall while using 35% fewer tokens at High effort reasoning mode and reducing the average cost per task by around 60%,” Alibaba
title: Alibaba touts 62% lower task costs with Qwen4-Max, adds cyber safeguards

description:
While AI agents, which can perform long-running work autonomously, have supplanted simple chats for serious work with large (and small) language models, agents have a last-mile problem: How do you display what an agent is doing in front of a user and let the user act on it, without forcing every team to build its own plumbing? One answer is AG-UI, which is intended to standardize how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience. It grew out of CopilotKit’s initial partnership with LangChain and CrewA
title: Getting started with AG-UI — the agent-user interaction protocol

description:
The conversation around AI governance is already happening. Organizations have spent the past few years accelerating AI adoption across software development. Now they face a different problem. AI systems can act faster than the organizations responsible for them can understand or govern what is happening.

Organizations are thinking about compliance, data privacy, security, and model reliability while boards are demanding policies and regulators are developing frameworks. title: How AI agents are changing the rules of software governance
